findings.title: `accepts_inline_and_file_ca` is now always ignored, so valid CA parsing is no longer tested.
findings.body: This test used to run offline with an embedded PEM and checked that a valid inline CA and a valid file CA are both accepted by the reqwest/rustls client. It now needs a real AKS CA in the environment and is marked `#[ignore]`. The only remaining offline CA tests are negative or use a mock factory. A change that makes valid PEM bundles fail would now pass CI. Fix: keep a non-ignored positive test that uses a CA generated at runtime (for example with rcgen or openssl under `client_certificate`).

findings.title: The only CI test of the real rustls CA and SNI client is replaced by a mock and an ignored test.
findings.body: Before this change, `sends_requests_with_custom_ca_and_sni` ran under `--all-features`. It started a local TLS server with a generated CA and checked that the built-in `reqwest::Client` factory trusted the custom CA, sent the expected SNI and kept the Host header. In this PR, the factory is replaced by `MockTokenProxyClient`, and the real test needs a live AKS identity binding pod (`#[ignore]`). As a result, nothing in CI now runs the code this PR changed: the `impl TokenProxyClient for reqwest::Client` builder, the root-certificate handling, `resolve_to_addrs` and `tls_backend_rustls`. A regression there would merge without any failing test. The issue (move `reqwest/rustls` into `reqwest_rustls`) did not ask for this. Fix: keep the local TLS-server test under `#[cfg(all(feature = "reqwest_rustls", feature = "client_certificate"))]`, generating the certificates at runtime as before.

findings.title: The IMDS live test is now permanently ignored, a test-infrastructure change the request does not cover.
findings.body: `imds_system_assigned_live` was a `#[recorded::test(live)]` test that ran in live pipelines and skipped itself when `IDENTITY_IMDS_AVAILABLE` was unset. It is now `#[ignore]` with plain `#[tokio::test]`, so live pipelines whose agents set `IDENTITY_IMDS_AVAILABLE` no longer run it at all. This file also drops the `CI_HAS_DEPLOYED_RESOURCES` skip guards. Issue #5550 only asks to move rustls to `reqwest_rustls`; these test-gating changes alter the live CI coverage and belong in a separate PR.

findings.title: The live-test provisioning script is rewritten, which the feature-flag fix does not need.
findings.body: This hunk changes how the shared test-resources post script works. It now decides whether to run from a new `IDENTITY_DEPLOY_RESOURCES` Bicep output instead of `AdditionalParameters`, and it runs `az account set` outside CI. `TenantId` and `Environment` are no longer mandatory. It adds readiness probes and HTTP polling that fail provisioning if authentication and storage access don't succeed within 180s (role propagation can take longer). It also uses a temporary kubeconfig and Dockerfile. Together with the new Bicep output, this changes live CI provisioning behaviour, and the request (move `reqwest/rustls` behind `reqwest_rustls`) gives no reason for it. Split it into its own PR so it can be reviewed and validated against the live pipeline.

held.title: `azure_core_test` now turns off all of `azure_identity`'s default features.
held.body: Adding `default-features = false` does more than avoid rustls. It also removes `azure_core/default` and `reqwest_rustls` from `azure_identity` as `azure_core_test` uses it. When `azure_core_test` is built on its own (for example `cargo build -p azure_core_test` or a published consumer), the credentials it builds for recording or live runs may have no default HTTP transport. I could not check whether another dependency re-enables these features. The request only concerns `azure_identity`'s own feature definitions. If the aim is just to stop forcing rustls, enable `features = ["reqwest"]` (or the features it actually needs) explicitly, or drop this change.
